newsitem.title: GERMANY: German winter crops thrive in ideal weather.
newsitem.headline: German winter crops thrive in ideal weather.

text.p: German crops were flourishing in favourable weather conditions with moist soil and cool temperatures for the time of year, the DWD meteorological office said.
"Temperatures are cool, but good enough to aid growth -- too much warmth would result in premature development," a DWD source said.
Barley, rye, wheat and rapeseed were all in the ground now but sowings of winter wheat will continue into the middle of December after the sugar beet harvest has been completed.
Beet harvests were speeding along while maize and sunseed harvests were in their final stages.
In Lower Saxony, farmers responding to a farm union survey said field work was now progressing after rainfall delayed work on heavy soils in the South of this key agricultural state.
Winter rye was developing well but barley growth had been slowed by cool temperatures, the farmers said.
National farm price office ZMP said farmers across the country had planned to extend winter rapeseed plantings by up to 35 percent over last year's 778,882 hectares.
But delays to the 1996 grain crop last month meant they would have been too late in trying to achieve this goal and a decline was more likely.
ZMP's eastern German branch reported sunseed yields from the 1996 crop were below average and high moisture content added to costs.

DWD forecast changeable weather and average maximum day temperatures in the week to Oct 30 of 10 degrees, having recorded seven to 12 degrees in the week Oct 17-23, with southwestern spikes of 16 degrees.
